A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InfiGFusion work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite added sections and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original fusion benchmark results, ablations, case studies, and teacher–student distillation experiments, including results in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds Gaussian simulations and comparisons of GW objectives on BBH subsets.

M1.justification: The proposed top-k graph construction, degree-feature compression, sorting-based matching, and combined GLD/ULD/SFT objective remain unchanged. The additional GW objectives and source-selection trials do not become components of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Section 4.7 adds synthetic Gaussian inputs for evaluating GW distance estimation. The fusion training datasets, eleven benchmarks, and appendix distillation datasets remain unchanged; the new Appendix G comparison reuses existing BBH tasks.

E2.justification: v2 introduces direct approximation comparisons with Exact GW and Sinkhorn GW in Section 4.7, and evaluates Sinkhorn GW and Entropic GW as alternative training objectives in Table 10. These substantially extend comparisons of the central approximation component. Existing fusion and distillation comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate Gaussian distance matrices across nine sample sizes from 50 to 3000 using estimation error and runtime, and compare three GW objectives on BBH subsets. Separately, Section 4.4 changes the stated ablation setting from top-k 30 to 10 while retaining the scores; this does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.7 and Appendix G add substantial analyses of approximation fidelity, computational scaling, and downstream performance under alternative GW objectives. Appendix J also reports marginal gains from preliminary entropy-based source-selection and Bayesian-alignment trials. Existing component ablations, top-k sensitivity, distribution plots, and case studies remain.

E5.justification: Section 4.7 explicitly reports simulation means and standard deviations, but inconsistently specifies three repetitions and five seeds. The new checklist states that significance calculations were not performed. Existing five-seed distillation reporting is unchanged; no increase in its run count is established.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports estimation errors and timings: at n=3000, approximation relative error is 0.3941 and runtime is 0.2408 seconds versus 52.8898 seconds for Exact GW. Table 10 adds distances, bound-derived relative errors, and downstream scores for three objectives. Matched pre-existing benchmark and distillation results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Propositions 1–2 and Appendices A–C retain the same approximation bound, assumptions, Lipschitz arguments, and proofs. The new relative-error calculations and empirical comparisons do not revise those derivations or establish a new theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same structure-aware fusion novelty, O(n log n) approximation guarantee, unchanged inference-cost claim, and eleven-benchmark reasoning claims. The added experiments address existing claims rather than redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix F.1 clarifies that 'internal reasoning' means logit relations without explicitly modeling reasoning steps. Appendix J expands the factual-conflict limitation and possible remedies. Section 4.7 and Appendix G add fidelity–cost interpretations. The original limitations paragraph is retained and relocated.

D1.justification: The model-access pointer changes from the Reallm-Labs GitHub repository to the InfiX-ai/InfiGFusion-14B Hugging Face checkpoint. Section 4.7 adds sampling and solver details, including the square-loss API and epsilon discussion. Appendix D's optimizer, hardware, loss weights, and offline-loading details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction newly emphasizes ULD as a representative cross-tokenizer approach, and Appendix J positions conflict-aware source selection as complementary to GLD. The 68 listed references otherwise match; ULD's move from reference 34 to 15 is renumbering, not a newly cited work.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 4.7, Appendices G and J, and a NeurIPS checklist; moves limitations before the references; and updates affiliations and the conference header. Most existing exposition, scientific section order, and proof prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the Gaussian-results table and the BBH GW-objective comparison table. All five existing figures and matched existing tables are retained, with changed placement and pagination; the distillation table moves to a standalone final page.

improvement.justification: The added approximation tests and clearer mechanism qualifications could strengthen v1's validation. However, the new evidence has unresolved inconsistencies: Section 4.7 alternates between three and five runs, and Table 10 reports 94.4% for Dyck Languages versus 40.0% in retained Tables 3 and 8 without explaining a setting difference. Because these issues affect the central new validation, the benefits and reporting harms do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
